developer: Fabio Sgarbossa, Mirco Peron (NTNU); Francesco Lolli, Elia Balugani (University of Modena and Reggio Emilia)
decision_levels: Part selection; Process/machine choice; Adopt or make-vs-buy
description: Periodic-review Poisson inventory model choosing manufacturing option, review period and order-up-to level, with technology-specific unit costs (from experts) and AM-vs-CM failure-rate ratios from fatigue literature; decision trees show backorder cost (~EUR 3,500/unit split) is the main driver and that AM wins whenever storage is zero.
NRE_note: Design/NRE explicitly not modeled (listed as future work).
Production_note: Expert-estimated unit production cost by technology, post-processing, part size and complexity for 316L.
QA_Qual_note: Qualification not modeled; reliability enters via literature fatigue ratios only.
QA_Insp_note: Inspection not modeled (post-processing such as HIP and polishing is in production cost).
Storage_note: Holding cost (30%/yr of unit cost) on expected stock; limited storage capacity (Smax) tested.
Shared_Capital_note: AM machine capacity and capital explicitly not modeled.
Shared_Capacity_note: Single-item, single-echelon; no capacity.
Speed_note: Backorder cost EUR 1,000-51,000/unit and technology-specific lead times; deterministic lead times.

name: Peron failure-rate-uncertainty AM vs CM spare parts model with inspection tools
developer: Mirco Peron, Andrea M. Coruzzolo, Rob Basten, Nils Knofius, Francesco Lolli, Fabio Sgarbossa
description: Periodic-review Poisson inventory model with materials-science-based failure-rate uncertainty showing AM is penalized far more than CM by uncertainty; porosity assessment or in-situ monitoring pays off only if it cuts uncertainty by ~5-6 percentage points.
NRE_note: Only the abstract was read and it does not mention design or other one-time engineering costs, so whether they are modeled is unknown.
Production_note: The abstract states AM's high production costs are weighed against inventory cost reductions, but the cost structure was not seen.
QA_Qual_note: Failure-rate uncertainty of AM parts (a qualification issue) is modeled; no certification cost.
QA_Insp_note: Porosity assessment and in-situ monitoring treated as investments with break-even uncertainty reduction (~5 and ~6 pp).
Storage_note: Periodic-review inventory; AM short lead time reduces inventory.
Shared_Capital_note: Only the abstract was read and it does not mention AM machine capital, so whether it is modeled is unknown.
Shared_Capacity_note: Only the abstract was read and it does not mention AM capacity, so whether it is modeled is unknown.
Speed_note: The abstract names AM's short lead time as the source of its inventory savings, but whether a backorder or downtime cost is in the model was not seen.

name: Cantini spare parts supply chain configuration DSS (AM vs CM, degree of centralization)
developer: Alessandra Cantini, Filippo De Carlo (University of Florence); Mirco Peron, Fabio Sgarbossa (NTNU)
description: Cost model (purchasing, ordering, holding, transport, backorders) over five degrees of stock centralization x AM/CM, run over 10,000 Sobol scenarios and distilled into a decision tree (77% accuracy at depth 4, 97% at depth 15); hybrid centralization most often optimal.
NRE_note: Digitalisation of AM items folded into supplier unit price (lump sum).
Production_note: AM and CM unit purchasing cost as lump-sum supplier price.
QA_Qual_note: Not modeled.
QA_Insp_note: Quality control activities embedded in supplier unit price (lump sum).
Storage_note: (s,Q) holding cost on cycle and safety stock per DC, times number of DCs.
Shared_Capital_note: Fixed AM/CM equipment costs embedded in supplier price; model uses only variable costs.
Shared_Capacity_note: Degree of centralization pools stock across DCs; AM production capacity not modeled (external supplier).
Speed_note: Backorder cost x expected backorders; supplier lead times (AM 1-4 wk, CM 4-26 wk) found to matter little.

name: Heinen-Hoberg portfolio-level AM switchover model
developer: J. Jakob Heinen, Kai Hoberg (Kuehne Logistics University, Hamburg)
description: Inventory-model-based portfolio analysis of which SKUs become cheaper to supply with AM given demand, TM fixed costs and minimum order quantities; at a 300% AM premium ~8% of SKUs (2% of units) switch, cutting system cost ~6.4%.
NRE_note: Only the abstract and introduction were read; they mention TM fixed costs but not AM one-time design or digitization costs, so whether these are modeled is unknown.
Production_note: AM unit cost as a multiplier of TM cost; no part-level structure.
QA_Qual_note: Only the abstract and introduction were read and they do not mention qualification, so whether it is modeled is unknown.
QA_Insp_note: Only the abstract and introduction were read and they do not mention inspection, so whether it is modeled is unknown.
Storage_note: Inventory from TM lot sizes and MOQs is the main cost driver AM removes.
Shared_Capital_note: Only the abstract and introduction were read and they do not mention AM machine capital, so whether it is modeled is unknown.
Shared_Capacity_note: Only the abstract and introduction were read and they do not mention AM capacity or network placement, so whether it is modeled is unknown.
Speed_note: Only the abstract and introduction were read and they do not mention lead time, backorders or downtime, so whether speed is valued is unknown.

name: Ahlsell automotive slow-moving spare parts AM supply chain cost model
developer: Levin Ahlsell, Didar Jalal, Patrik Jonsson (Chalmers); Siavash H. Khajavi, Jan Holmstrom (Aalto)
description: Total supply chain cost model (production price, inbound/outbound transport, ABC-based warehousing, and service costs incl. vehicle-off-road downtime, badwill, lost sales) over the part life cycle; 3 of 14 parts show savings; metal AM parts cost ~1,756% more and need 72-99% cost cuts to break even.
NRE_note: Not modeled; supplier quotes only.
Production_note: Part-specific supplier quotes per technology, but a lump-sum price with no build-up.
QA_Qual_note: Not modeled.
QA_Insp_note: Not modeled.
Storage_note: Warehousing (capital, handling, overhead via ABC) and MOQ-driven excess/scrap modeled.
Shared_Capital_note: Outsourced; machine capital embedded in price.
Shared_Capacity_note: Only centralized outsourced AM modeled; decentralized discussed qualitatively.
Speed_note: Vehicle-off-road (VOR) downtime cost plus badwill and lost sales, split by in-stock/out-of-stock cases.

name: Cokyasar-Jin AM capacity allocation problem (AMCAP) over a network
developer: Taner Cokyasar, Mingzhou Jin
decision_levels: Part selection; Adopt or make-vs-buy; Capacity placement/sharing
description: Mixed-integer nonlinear program assigning each part to on-demand AM at a facility or an alternative source (e.g., inventory), sizing AM capacity, with convex nonlinear waiting time at each AM facility; optimal deployment saves ~20% vs no AM.
NRE_note: Only the abstract was read and it does not mention design, digitization or other one-time costs, so whether they are modeled is unknown.
Production_note: The abstract states production cost is a term in the objective, but its structure was not seen.
QA_Qual_note: Only the abstract was read and it does not mention qualification, so whether it is modeled is unknown.
QA_Insp_note: Only the abstract was read and it does not mention inspection, so whether it is modeled is unknown.
Storage_note: The abstract names inventory holding as the alternative sourcing option whose cost is in the objective, but its formulation was not seen.
Shared_Capital_note: Number of AM machines per facility is optimized against machine cost (sensitivity on machine cost and build speed).
Shared_Capacity_note: Capacity allocation across facilities with load-dependent waiting time (queueing) at each AM facility.
Speed_note: Lead-time cost is an explicit objective term.

name: Strong two-stage p-median model for metal AM post-processing hubs
developer: Danielle Strong, Michael Kay, Brett Conner, Thomas Wakefield, Guha Manogharan (Penn State and collaborators)
description: Two-stage p-median facility location model choosing hub locations and capacities and assigning demand across machine shops and heat-treatment facilities, minimizing fixed, operating and transport costs; 22 hubs grow to 35 as demand rises.
NRE_note: Only the abstract was read and it does not mention design or engineering costs, so whether they are modeled is unknown.
Production_note: Operating costs at hubs; not part-level.
QA_Qual_note: Only the abstract was read and it does not mention qualification, so whether it is modeled is unknown.
QA_Insp_note: Only the abstract was read; it covers heat treatment and machining but does not say whether inspection is costed.
Storage_note: Only the abstract was read and it does not mention inventory, so whether it is modeled is unknown.
Shared_Capital_note: Fixed hub costs vs number of hubs traded off in the p-median objective.
Shared_Capacity_note: Hub capacity and utilization with demand assignment; effect on lead time not modeled.
Speed_note: Only the abstract was read and it does not mention lead time or delivery time, so whether speed is valued is unknown.

name: Barz two-stage capacitated facility location model with AM buy-to-fly ratio
developer: Andreas Barz, Tobias Buer, Hans-Dietrich Haasis
description: Two-stage capacitated facility location problem showing that lower buy-to-fly ratios (AM) cut transport costs and shift production sites closer to customers, with the site count roughly unchanged.
NRE_note: Not modeled.
Production_note: Production costs explicitly excluded.
QA_Qual_note: Not modeled.
QA_Insp_note: Not modeled.
Storage_note: Storage at sites forbidden; no inventory.
Shared_Capital_note: Fixed cost of opening production sites, not AM machine capital.
Shared_Capacity_note: Site capacities and customer assignment; no lead-time effect.
Speed_note: Not modeled.

name: Doudnikoff NCSU/USMA military spare parts network model (extends McDermott et al.)
developer: Letai M. Doudnikoff (advisor Brandon M. McConnell), North Carolina State University
earlier_versions: McDermott, Winz, Hodgson, Kay, King & McConnell 2021 (Journal of Defense Analytics and Logistics 5(2):179; from McDermott's 2020 NCSU MS thesis, with the Winz et al. 2020 readiness-vs-cost working paper): the original Monte Carlo + Croston/SBA intermittent-demand + MILP (s,S) model comparing no-AM, centralized and distributed AM. It found centralized AM wins for lumpy demand and distributed for stable demand. Doudnikoff 2021 reuses this model and its 1-1-4 network and modifies it for isolated military sustainment networks, first-machine placement and AM fixed-cost/capacity trade-offs.
description: MILP inventory policy plus Monte Carlo simulation (60 periods) for first-machine placement and isolated-network studies; distributed first machine lowers operating and transport cost, but no-AM is cheapest once AM fixed cost is included; returns to added AM capacity diminish.
NRE_note: Not modeled.
Production_note: AM production cost assumed equal to TM.
QA_Qual_note: Build quality assumed equal to TM.
QA_Insp_note: Not modeled.
Storage_note: Inventory carrying cost and MILP order-up-to levels; Markov-bootstrap reorder points.
Shared_Capital_note: AM fixed cost per machine per day ($121, $241 and $512 in Table 3.1, with sensitivity) decides whether AM pays at all; the $2,000-5,000 metal-machine figure is only a footnote citing outside research.
Shared_Capacity_note: AM capacity per node per period; centralized vs distributed placement; network redundancy; diminishing returns to capacity.
Speed_note: Backorder penalties; lead time to the isolated DC drives reorder points and backorders.

name: Einhorn distributed AM operational-readiness model (NPS, Army)
developer: MAJ Matthew T. Einhorn, USA (Naval Postgraduate School; advisors Matthew G. Boensel, Paul Beery)
description: Uses Ao = MTBM/(MTBM+MDT) with logistics delay time by AM placement, plus timed print experiments (printing ~96% of AM time, ~10% first-print failures), to show AM at the SSA lets an AM part have ~1/3 the MTBM of a conventional part while keeping Ao at 0.90.
NRE_note: Not modeled.
Production_note: Cost explicitly out of scope; only print/process times measured.
QA_Qual_note: Derives the minimum reliability (MTBM) an AM part needs to keep Ao, a qualification-relevant target; no qualification cost.
QA_Insp_note: Not modeled.
Storage_note: Not modeled.
Shared_Capital_note: Qualitative: equipment, personnel and material costs limit placement; larger printers justified where more customers are served.
Shared_Capacity_note: Compares AM placement echelons by logistics delay; no capacity or queue modeled.
Speed_note: Operational availability quantified via reduced mean downtime from AM placement (availability, not dollars).

name: Coyle naval aviation AM sustainment screening + DES (NPS)
developer: David M. Coyle (Naval Postgraduate School)
description: Top-down screen of Navy aviation inventory for AM candidates followed by an Innoslate discrete-event simulation (adapted from Jedeck 2015) comparing local stock, OEM order and local AM for one part: AM $3,145 in ~10 days vs OEM $7,005 in 545 days; at quarter print speed AM costs 17% more but stays far faster.
NRE_note: Assumes CAD/TDP exists; flags omitted reverse-engineering cost/time as possibly decisive and recommends PLM/digital thread.
Production_note: Per-part build-up: machine run cost ($550 for 18.6 h build), feedstock, setup ($100), removal ($100), post-processing ($1,000); print-speed sensitivity.
QA_Qual_note: Qualification time for reverse-engineered parts identified as a gap; not modeled.
QA_Insp_note: Final inspection included ($400, 1 day).
Storage_note: Local inventory holding cost (10% of unit cost per year).
Shared_Capital_note: Machine time priced via a run rate; no analysis of sharing/utilization.
Shared_Capacity_note: Single local machine; no network or queue.
Speed_note: Procurement and administrative lead time are the central screening weights, and the DES quantifies AM vs. conventional supply times. Readiness (NMCS) is the framing, but it is not dollarized.

name: Veitenheimer AFIT centralized vs distributed AM Monte Carlo (EOD robots)
developer: Capt Shane R. Veitenheimer, USAF (Air Force Institute of Technology)
description: Excel/VBA Monte Carlo (10,000 trials) of repair-part costs and intratheater shipping under centralized (Bagram depot) vs distributed AM, converting annual savings to NPV over 3-10 year machine lives to back-solve the justifiable printer price (~$72.8k-232.7k centralized/full down to ~$520-1,690 distributed/limited).
NRE_note: Not modeled.
Production_note: Benefit valued as avoided repair-part purchase cost; AM production cost not modeled.
QA_Qual_note: Not modeled.
QA_Insp_note: Not modeled.
Storage_note: Inventory carrying and obsolescence explicitly excluded.
Shared_Capital_note: NPV-based justifiable machine price for one shared central machine vs one per site.
Shared_Capacity_note: Centralized vs distributed scenarios with intratheater air shipping cost; no capacity or queue.
Speed_note: Downtime explicitly excluded.

name: NPS data-farming simulations of expeditionary AM logistics and Ao (NPS-LM-22-006, 2022)
developer: Susan M. Sanchez, Claudia Luhrs, Mary L. McDonald, Maj Greg Lynch USMC (Naval Postgraduate School, Acquisition Research Program)
earlier_versions: Sanchez, Lynch, Luhrs & McDonald (2019) 'Networked Logistics and Additive Manufacturing', Acquisition Research Symposium slides SYM-AM-19-156: earlier presentation of the data-farmed 'Iron Network' AM simulation; the 2022 report is the full write-up and includes the operational availability model.
description: Discrete-event simulations with nearly-orthogonal Latin hypercube data farming: AM factors had small effects on network delivery performance, but in the Ao model (notional data) AM parts raised days with >=42 operational vehicles from 13% to 79% with fewer maintainers and vehicles.
NRE_note: Not modeled.
Production_note: No cost model.
QA_Qual_note: AM reliability multiplier (0.5-2.0) explored; QA, liability and training costs listed only qualitatively.
QA_Insp_note: Not modeled.
Storage_note: Storage volume/logistics footprint and inventory visibility discussed; not costed.
Shared_Capital_note: Not modeled.
Shared_Capacity_note: AM placement across echelons simulated; printer capacity and speed not varied.
Speed_note: Operational availability quantified (13% vs 79% of days meeting fleet goal); request turnaround times.

name: NPS KVA / real-options make-or-buy model for Navy ship parts (3DP + 3D scanning + CPLM)
developer: David Ford (Texas A&M); Tom Housel, Sandra Hom, Johnathan Mun (Naval Postgraduate School)
description: Knowledge Value Added ROI, Monte Carlo volatility and real options compare make/buy mixes by part complexity; all-Navy production estimated to save ~$12.7M/yr per depot (~$120M across 10 depots), with a phased compound option most valuable.
NRE_note: 3D laser scanning (digitization) included as enabler, but costs come only from aggregate KVA ROI, not a structured NRE term.
Production_note: Costs back-derived from assumed part values ($1k-6k by complexity) and KVA ROI; no geometry/material/machine structure.
QA_Qual_note: Not modeled.
QA_Insp_note: Not modeled.
Storage_note: Not modeled.
Shared_Capital_note: Real options value phased investment in the technologies; no machine amortization or utilization.
Shared_Capacity_note: Not modeled.
Speed_note: Shorter in-sourced cycle times linked to fleet readiness; not dollarized in the model.

name: Jedeck spare-parts-on-demand AM vs warehousing simulation (Arena)
developer: Stefan Jedeck (University of Louisville)
decision_levels: Process/machine choice; Adopt or make-vs-buy; Capacity placement/sharing
description: Arena discrete-event simulation routing each request through parallel warehousing and AM paths to compare costs under varied build speed, build volume, material price, machine price, cool-down, and multi-machine/multi-material strategies.
NRE_note: Pre-work/CAD preparation assumed complete.
Production_note: Material price, build time/speed, build volume, setup and cool-down, operator cost, machine price and depreciation.
QA_Qual_note: Not modeled.
QA_Insp_note: Rework/finishing only as process time.
Storage_note: Stock value, 13% storage cost, EOQ/reorder point.
Shared_Capital_note: Machine purchase price/depreciation spread across all requests; multi-machine strategies.
Shared_Capacity_note: Yes. Queueing, priority rules and build-volume batching at a shared AM site set delivery time. Single site (1 to 3 machines), no cross-site pooling.
Speed_note: Late-delivery penalties in cost.

name: O'Brien aerospace spare parts AM shop DES vs warehouse model
developer: Kyle O'Brien (University of Louisville)
description: Discrete-event simulation of AM machines and operators benchmarked against an inventory-theory warehouse model; AM saves money when late-delivery penalties are high, and adding machines beats adding operators.
NRE_note: Only the abstract was read and it does not mention design, CAD or reverse-engineering cost, so whether it is modeled is unknown.
Production_note: The abstract names production cost as a DES output under different production policies, but its structure was not seen.
QA_Qual_note: Only the abstract was read and it does not mention qualification or build failures, so whether they are modeled is unknown.
QA_Insp_note: Only the abstract was read and it does not mention inspection, so whether it is modeled is unknown.
Storage_note: Warehouse inventory model from established inventory theory as benchmark.
Shared_Capital_note: The abstract compares adding machines versus operators but does not say whether machine purchase cost or depreciation is in the cost model.
Shared_Capacity_note: Yes. Shared machine and operator capacity, utilisation and queue re-sequencing against due dates set lead time. Single AM shop, no cross-site pooling.
Speed_note: Late-delivery penalty costs drive AM savings.

name: Abidar-Chaabane METRIC model with centralized/decentralized AM repair
developer: Youssef Abidar, Amin Chaabane (Ecole de technologie superieure, Montreal)
description: METRIC scenarios with AM at the central centre vs at regional centres, varying AM repair time and probability by demand class; decentralized AM best when AM is faster, or equally fast with >70% AM repair probability; slow/non-moving parts most suitable.
NRE_note: Not modeled.
Production_note: AM operating cost not modeled.
QA_Qual_note: Not modeled.
QA_Insp_note: Not modeled.
Storage_note: Stock levels varied as service lever; holding cost not modeled.
Shared_Capital_note: AM machine investment not modeled.
Shared_Capacity_note: Central vs regional AM placement compared; AM capacity limits not modeled.
Speed_note: Expected backorders per configuration, converted to dollars via unit price.

name: Busachi/Erkoyuncu (Cranfield, Babcock) AM framework and decision support for Royal Navy support services
developer: Alessandro Busachi, John Erkoyuncu, Paul Colegrove (Cranfield University); Richard Drake, Chris Watts, Stephen Wilding (Babcock International)
decision_levels: Part selection; Process/machine choice; Adopt or make-vs-buy; Capacity placement/sharing
description: Soft-systems framework with eight phases (mission, platform, configuration, critical-to-availability parts, AM technology, DfAM, manufacturing configuration, dynamic simulation) and availability equations in which on-platform AM removes administrative and procurement delay; authors state benefits still need quantification.
NRE_note: Geometry preparation and bidding are costed cost-breakdown elements (Procedia CIRP 2018); 3D scanning for parts with no CAD file (reverse engineering) and redesign are part of the framework (IJSAEM 2018).
Production_note: Rate-based cost model (machine, software, human resources) plus AM time and cost models (Procedia CIRP 2018; thesis abstract).
QA_Qual_note: Part qualification identified as the main constraint; not quantified.
QA_Insp_note: 3D-scanner quality assurance is a costed element in the FDM demonstrator; WAAM NDT methods (X-ray, ultrasound, neutron diffraction) are listed qualitatively (Procedia CIRP 2018/2015).
Storage_note: Lower platform inventory and freed space cited qualitatively.
Shared_Capital_note: Machine rate includes investment, utilisation time and rate, and overheads (Procedia CIRP 2018).
Shared_Capacity_note: 21 AM location configurations rated qualitatively on cost, speed and security.
Speed_note: Availability and logistic delay time are explicit simulation/DSS outputs [1][2].

name: Strieby USMC expeditionary metal AM cost-effectiveness analysis
developer: LtCol Stephen F. Strieby, USMC (Naval Postgraduate School, Acquisition Research Program)
description: Cost-effectiveness ratio (total system cost / parts produced over a 5-year life, from representative print times) for four metal AM processes with sensitivity on print and sintering times; recommends hybrid wire-arc AM.
NRE_note: Not modeled.
Production_note: Average cost per part from system cost and representative print times; not part-specific.
QA_Qual_note: Not modeled.
QA_Insp_note: Not modeled.
Storage_note: Logistics-footprint reduction is motivation only.
Shared_Capital_note: Acquisition and ownership costs amortized over parts produced in a 5-year life.
Shared_Capacity_note: Not modeled.
Speed_note: Benefit measured as parts produced; print speed key sensitivity; readiness explicitly not monetized.

name: NASA-STD-6030 Additive Manufacturing Requirements for Spaceflight Systems (2021)
developer: NASA (Marshall Space Flight Center; NASA Engineering and Safety Center)
earlier_versions: MSFC-STD-3716 (2017): Marshall standard for L-PBF spaceflight hardware; superseded by NASA-STD-6030 in 2021, which extended it to other AM processes. | MSFC-SPEC-3717 (2017): Marshall specification for control and qualification of L-PBF metallurgical processes; superseded in 2021 by NASA-STD-6030 and companion NASA-SPEC-6033.
description: Classifies each AM part by consequence of failure (Class A/B/C, plus Exempt), then structural demand and a points-based AM risk score (inspectability, removable as-built surfaces, supports, wall thickness) into subclasses A1–A4/B1–B4, and tailors the QA requirements (QMP, material property suite, witness testing, NDE, preproduction articles, part process qualification) to each class.
NRE_note: Requires a registered Qualified Metallurgical Process (QMP, per machine), a Part Production Plan and a Qualified Part Process, so parameter development and build preparation are mandatory deliverables, but none is costed (NASA-STD-6030 Sec. 5, 7, 8).
Production_note: No per-part production cost content; the standard is a requirements document (NASA-STD-6030).
QA_Qual_note: Prescribes qualification activities by class: full vs reduced QMP; statistically based material property suite for A/B vs simplified for C; preproduction articles required for A/B and removed for C; NASA attendance at the AM Readiness Review only for A1/A2. These are countable activities, but the standard gives no costs (Sec. 4.3, 4.15, 5, 6).
QA_Insp_note: Requires quantitative full surface and volumetric NDE for Class A (AMR-17) and removes NDE for Class C. Witness testing is set per Tables 5–8 for A/B, and Class C needs two tensile coupons per production build. Continuous production gets reduced witness sampling (Sec. 4.8, 4.11). The witness tables were not fully read.
Storage_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capital_note: Explicitly spreads one-time qualification across parts: a QMP is registered to a machine, and a lot-mature material property suite applies to any part of any class built under an equivalently controlled QMP. Sub-QMPs allow reduced testing. NASA briefings hope NRE per new program will be 'dramatically reduced' by a shared AM ecosystem. All of this is qualitative (Sec. 3.2; Glendening et al. 2021).
Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.
Speed_note: Schedule mentioned only qualitatively ('building this foundation can take years'; witness tests 'can take considerable time') in the 2021 NASA QLF briefing.

name: ISO/ASTM 52967:2024 part classifications for AM parts used in aviation
developer: ASTM Committee F42 / ISO TC 261 (joint)
earlier_versions: ASTM F3572-22 (2022): original ASTM practice with the same four consequence-of-failure classes (A-D); still listed as active by ASTM; published as joint ISO/ASTM 52967 in 2024 (valid from Oct 2024).
description: Assigns aviation AM parts to Class A (high), B (medium), C (low) or D (negligible) by consequence of failure. The class is meant as a common metric that downstream material, process, NDI and qualification specifications use to set levels of process control, post-processing, qualification and inspection.
NRE_note: Not addressed (F3572 scope).
Production_note: Not addressed.
QA_Qual_note: The class is explicitly intended to set qualification levels in downstream documents, but the standard does not prescribe what each class requires (F3572 scope and intended-use text; ISO/ASTM 52967 introduction).
QA_Insp_note: Same logic: classes are a metric for NDI and testing levels, but no inspection activities are prescribed per class.
Storage_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capital_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.
Speed_note: Not addressed.

name: USAF Structures Bulletin EZ-SB-19-01: Durability and Damage Tolerance Certification for AM Aircraft Structural Metallic Parts
developer: U.S. Air Force, AFLCMC/EZ (Engineering Directorate)
description: Sets durability and damage-tolerance certification requirements for metal AM structural parts by ASIP category (Fracture Critical Traceable/Non-Traceable, Durability Critical, Normal Controls), using equivalent initial damage size at category-specific exceedance probabilities and validated NDI capability. It recommends gaining experience in order of escalating criticality (NC, then DC, then FC).
NRE_note: Requires demonstrated process control (equipment qualification, software version control, periodic requalification, frozen process), which implies parameter development, but this is not costed (EZ-SB-19-01 process control section).
Production_note: Not addressed; cost appears only as stability/supportability criteria ('predictable costs', 'cost-effective' inspection).
QA_Qual_note: Sets class-specific analysis criteria: EIDS exceedance of 1e-1 (NC) and 1e-3 (DC), plus damage-tolerance analysis with a 1e-7 rogue EIDS for FC. All test frequencies, EIDS test counts and dissection plans are 'as approved by the procuring agency', so the qualification campaign by class cannot be costed from the bulletin.
QA_Insp_note: For all AM parts, requires NDI with POD at 95% confidence, dissection or validated in-process monitoring, coupons from production parts, and dimensional checks. These are not differentiated by part category, and frequencies are left to the procuring agency, so per-part inspection cannot be costed from the document.
Storage_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capital_note: Recommends building certification experience from NC to DC to FC parts, each stage reusing earlier data, so qualification data is implicitly reused across parts. Not costed.
Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.
Speed_note: Only says sustainment NDI should be available 'in a timely manner'.

name: USAF Flight Systems Bulletin EN-FSB-25-01 (Preliminary Qualification Data Requirements for Metallic AM) and Part Family Qualification approach
year: Unknown (bulletin number suggests 2025; the public abstract gives no date)
developer: U.S. Air Force (approach presented by M. Benedict at TMS 2026; issuing office not stated in the public abstract)
description: Separates material qualification from part certification and defines a standard minimum data set for screening new AM processes, materials and vendors on stability, producibility and predictability. It replaces 'point qualification' of each part with 'Part Family Qualification'.
NRE_note: The bulletin's documented scope is preliminary material, process and vendor qualification data, which excludes one-time part engineering.
Production_note: Not described.
QA_Qual_note: Defines a screening data set and a staged qualification logic to decide whether further qualification investment is worthwhile. No costs given (TMS 2026 abstract only).
QA_Insp_note: Only a conference abstract was read; the data requirements could include NDI, but the abstract does not say.
Storage_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capital_note: Explicitly moves from requalifying each part after any machine or process change to Part Family Qualification, which spreads qualification across a family of parts. Qualitative only.
Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.
Speed_note: Spare-part lead time is the motivation, but it is not valued in the method (abstract).

name: NAVSEA AM qualification framework: Guidance letter Ser 05T/2018-024 severity levels, T9074-AX-GIB-010/100 material selection requirements, and PBF/DED Technical Publications
year: 2018 (guidance letter); 2020 (PBF Tech Pub); 2021 (DED Tech Pub, anticipated)
developer: Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA 05T, AM Technical Warrant Holder); DED tech pub developed with NSWC Carderock and EWI
description: Part failure-consequence severity (NAVSEA 5100.12-M Levels 1–7/N/A) determines whether material selection requirements and process/material qualification apply, whether a Technical Data Package is needed, and who approves. The process Tech Pubs then prescribe procedure qualification, part verification builds and a production conformance test plan.
NRE_note: A DED Procedure defining essential variables must be NAVSEA-approved before testing, and a TDP is required for Levels 1–6. Not costed (Hovanec 2021; Ser 05T/2018-024).
Production_note: Not in the framework. NAVSEA says NAVSUP's separate cost/part tool is being integrated into TDP development (Rettaliata 2020); see Spillover.
QA_Qual_note: Levels 1–5 invoke T9074-AX-GIB-010/100 and process/material qualification, and Levels 1–6 need a risk assessment that sets the approval authority (High: COMNAVSEA/CHENG ... Low: waterfront CHENG). The Tech Pub steps are countable: procedure qualification build, PQTR, sacrificial part verification build with witness coupons, and test reports. No costs.
QA_Insp_note: NDE is set by material group with MIL-STD-2035 Class 1 acceptance; production NDE and destructive-test schedules are defined per part in each Production Conformance Evaluation Plan, not by severity level. In-situ monitoring in place of NDE is a stated goal (Rettaliata 2017).
Storage_note: Not addressed in the framework.
Shared_Capital_note: Explicit: procedure qualification is done once per process/material combination and applies to any geometry if essential elements are kept, so it spreads across parts. Not costed (Hovanec 2021).
Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.
Speed_note: The guidance letter says only qualitatively that AM 'can shorten the design-to-production cycle'.

name: DNV-ST-B203 Additive manufacturing (Edition 2025-11)
year: 2017 (DNVGL-CG-0197); first ST-B203 edition reported as 2019 (not confirmed); editions Dec 2022 and 2025-11
developer: DNV (formerly DNV GL)
earlier_versions: DNVGL-CG-0197 (2017): class guideline on AM qualification and certification; testing extent set by criticality, no per-category counts; read in full. | DNVGL-ST-B203 Additive manufacturing of metallic parts, first edition (year Unknown): covered two metal AM technologies. | DNV-ST-B203 edition of Dec 2022: added DED-arc, PBF-EB and binder jetting, combined manufacturing, NDT acceptance criteria, and guidance on part families and AMC selection; the 2025-11 edition adds polymers, a CO2 footprint method and grouped part approvals.
description: Assigns parts to AM categories AMC 1–3 by criticality (an informative appendix guides AMC selection). The category sets the qualification route: AMC 1 needs a facility audit and a build process qualification, and AMC 2/3 add part family qualification. Appendices give inspection/test plans and NDT guidance.
NRE_note: Has an informative appendix on part design, and build process qualification fixes the build process. Not costed (DNV ST-B203 page).
Production_note: Not addressed (the 2025 edition adds a carbon footprint appendix, not cost).
QA_Qual_note: The category determines countable qualification steps (AMC 1: facility audit plus at least one BPQ; AMC 2/3: plus part family qualification), per DNV certification-services slides. CG-0197 says testing extent depends on criticality and calls part-by-part certification 'costly, time consuming'. No figures. The exact AMC criteria were not seen.
QA_Insp_note: Peron, Cantini & Coruzzolo (2023) built a cost model on DNV-ST-B203. They show production testing that varies by class (C1 visual only; C2 and C3 add per-build tensile, impact, visual, surface and volumetric NDT and a dimensional check; C3 also adds part qualification) and price it per test, so inspection by category can be costed. The standard itself is paywalled.
Storage_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capital_note: The manufacturer is qualified once per AMC level, and part family qualification covers multiple parts, which spreads qualification. Qualitative.
Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.
Speed_note: Not addressed.

name: API Standard 20S Additively Manufactured Metallic Components (AM Specification Levels AMSL 1/2/3)
developer: American Petroleum Institute
description: Specifies process qualification and production control for AM metallic components at three AM Specification Levels. Each higher level raises technical, quality and qualification requirements, and the level is assigned by the product specification, purchaser or manufacturer according to consequence of failure, service severity and inspectability.
NRE_note: Only summaries were seen; API says the standard covers manufacturing-process qualification and was written to optimize component design, so whether it treats one-time engineering such as build-procedure development is not established.
Production_note: Not addressed.
QA_Qual_note: Qualification requirements scale with AMSL (GlobalSpec abstract), but the per-level activities were not verified because the full text was not accessed. The standard may meet the 'Yes' bar.
QA_Insp_note: Testing/NDE scale with AMSL per summaries. Specifics not verified (Inspenet summary; GlobalSpec).
Storage_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capital_note: Only summaries were seen, so whether the standard lets one process qualification cover several parts (for example part families) is not established.
Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.
Speed_note: The scope (process qualification, production, marking and documentation requirements) excludes lead-time valuation; API cites shorter lead times only as a motivation.

name: FAA AM Roadmap and risk-based certification framework (Gorelik briefings)
developer: Federal Aviation Administration (AM National Team; M. Gorelik, Chief Scientist for Fatigue and Damage Tolerance)
description: Ties regulatory scrutiny to part criticality and maps the qualification path to criticality and volume: point-design certification for low-criticality, high-margin parts; part-family qualification as volume grows; model-enabled qualification later. It gives indicative figures for the barrier to entry and qualification timelines.
NRE_note: Process development is lumped into a barrier-to-entry estimate (about $1M for equipment alone vs '$10's of M' realistic, including process development, qualification, controls, characterization, design data and QA/NDI). Indicative only (Gorelik 2016, 2017).
Production_note: Not addressed.
QA_Qual_note: Qualitative criticality-to-qualification-path mapping, plus indicative magnitudes: new aerospace alloy introduction takes 10–15 years, and modifying an existing material for a critical structural part up to 4 years. A building-block test cost table was only partly legible. Not a model.
QA_Insp_note: Lists NDI capability as a top-5 challenge, proposes probabilistic fracture mechanics using inspection POD and zone-based evaluation instead of casting factors, and in-process QA. No costs.
Storage_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capital_note: Recommends moving to part-family-based qualification as volumes increase, which implicitly spreads qualification over more parts. Qualitative.
Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.
Speed_note: Not addressed.

name: CMU adaptive regulatory framework for metal AM in aviation (Bonnín Roca et al. 2017)
developer: Carnegie Mellon University, Engineering and Public Policy (with Universidade de Lisboa / CMU Portugal)
earlier_versions: Bonnín Roca, Fuchs, Morgan & Vaishnav 2016, 'Policy needed for additive manufacturing' (Nature Materials commentary): earlier call for process science, standards and adaptive regulation that the 2017 paper develops into a framework.
description: Uses metal AM in aviation as a case study to propose adaptive regulation: standards revised periodically, and firms regulated differently according to their technological capabilities. It gives a general framework in which the right regulatory design depends on industry structure, safety requirements and sources of technological uncertainty.
NRE_note: The framework concerns how regulators set certification requirements for firms of differing capability; one-time part engineering is outside its documented scope.
Production_note: The framework is a regulatory-policy design; per-part production cost is outside its documented scope.
QA_Qual_note: Qualitative policy framework for how certification burden should be set under uncertainty and differ by firm capability. No costs (Research Policy 2017 abstract).
QA_Insp_note: Only abstracts were read; the papers address certification standards, so whether they treat inspection or NDE requirements is not established.
Storage_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capital_note: Only abstracts were read; regulating firms by capability could let one qualification carry across parts or users, but no source shows the papers treating this.
Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.
Speed_note: Not addressed.

name: Rapid qualification framework for powder-bed laser AM parts (Honeywell-led DARPA Open Manufacturing work; Peralta et al.)
developer: Honeywell Aerospace-led team (Peralta, Enright, Megahed, Gong, Roybal, Craig) under DARPA Open Manufacturing
description: A probabilistic, risk-based qualification framework that runs ICME models (melt pool CFD, residual stress/distortion FE, microstructure/strength) with Bayesian calibration in a digital loop, adding physical tests only when the digital results do not show acceptable risk. In-situ monitoring and NDE feed the risk calculation.
NRE_note: ICME process models support parameter and build design (distortion, melt pool), but engineering effort is not costed.
Production_note: Not addressed.
QA_Qual_note: Targets 40% less qualification time and 20% less cost, and projects up to 40% fewer tests with certification-by-analysis rising from 10% to 20%. These are goals and projections, not a cost model; no dollar figures.
QA_Insp_note: Pyrometer/melt-pool imaging quality metrics against a 95% UCL flag off-nominal layers, and CT/acoustic microscopy detect porosity and feed the risk calculation. Authors say in-process data alone cannot accept a part. No cost.
Storage_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capital_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.
Speed_note: Qualification time target only; part lead time not valued.

name: NIST qualification pathways for AM materials, processes and parts (statistical, equivalence-based, model-based, 'qualify-as-you-go')
year: 2014-2025 (project page created March 2014; project completed; page last updated March 2025)
developer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
description: Frames three qualification routes with different testing burdens and develops measurement science (round-robin protocols, a public materials database, validated process models, in-process measurement) to make equivalence and model-based qualification viable and to spread the cost of statistical testing.
NRE_note: Not addressed.
Production_note: Not addressed.
QA_Qual_note: Qualitative comparison of route burdens. Cites full empirical qualification as 'many thousands of individual tests', 'millions of dollars and 5 to 15 years' (NIST project page). No model.
QA_Insp_note: 'Qualify as you go' uses pre-, in- and post-process measurements to show each part meets spec. Concept only.
Storage_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capital_note: Explicitly aims to spread the cost of statistical qualification testing across many contributors via round-robin protocols and a public materials database. This shares qualification cost across users; qualitative.
Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.
Speed_note: Not addressed.

name: Seifi et al. qualification and certification pathway review (JOM, 2017)
developer: Seifi, Salem, Beuth, Harrysson, Lewandowski (2016); Seifi, Gorelik, Waller, Hrabe, Shamsaei, Daniewicz, Lewandowski (2017)
earlier_versions: Seifi et al. 2016, Overview of Materials Qualification Needs for Metal Additive Manufacturing (JOM 68, doi:10.1007/s11837-015-1810-0): companion review; source of the AMS4999A test counts and the 'millions of dollars, up to 15 years' figure.
description: Compares statistically based qualification (e.g., AMS4999A), model-based qualification and ICME 'qualify-as-you-go' schemes for metal AM. The 2017 paper maps the standards landscape needed for a Q&C pathway and cites NASA's AM risk criteria (inspectability, surface removal, wall thickness).
NRE_note: Not addressed.
Production_note: Not addressed.
QA_Qual_note: Gives costable test counts: AMS4999A requires >50 tensile results per principal build direction at source qualification and >12 per direction for production-part qualification. Also says legacy statistical qualification 'may cost millions of dollars and take up to 15 years' and that deviations trigger requalification (2016). Not a model.
QA_Insp_note: Discusses micro-CT (10–20 µm resolution), the lack of AM NDT consensus standards at the time, and in-situ monitoring 'still in its infancy'. No costs.
Storage_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capital_note: The 2016 paper (full text) does not treat sharing qualification, but only the abstract and preview of the 2017 standardization review were read, so whether it discusses shared data or round-robins is not established.
Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.
Speed_note: Not addressed.

name: Cost model for the economic evaluation of in-situ monitoring tools in metal AM (Colosimo, Cavalli, Grasso)
developer: Politecnico di Milano
description: A per-part cost model comparing as-is production, in-situ monitoring, and monitoring with diagnosis. It uses scrap fraction, false-alarm and missed-detection rates, inspection time and monitoring equipment cost to find the scrap rates at which monitoring pays off, including a make-or-buy variant.
NRE_note: The full paper states that CAD development cost is not included and has no parameter-development term; build preparation is a recurring per-build cost.
Production_note: Computes per-part cost (e.g., 212.74 vs 192.99 EUR/part as-is vs monitoring), validated within about 10% of a service-bureau benchmark.
QA_Qual_note: Qualification and certification not modeled.
QA_Insp_note: Explicitly models scrap fraction, Type I/II error rates, post-process quality inspection (CMM/visual) time and cost, and 50k/150k EUR monitoring hardware. Finds break-even scrap fractions of about 0.02–0.2 depending on part value and detection performance, and about 9.3% average saving. CT cost explicitly excluded.
Storage_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capital_note: Upgraded on opening the manuscript: the L-PBF system is charged at an hourly rate from straight-line depreciation plus maintenance and space (case: EUR 600k over 5 years at a 55% load factor), and build cost is divided by parts per build, so machine capital is amortized into per-part cost.
Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.
Speed_note: Not addressed.

name: Process-based cost estimation model for metal AM spare parts with explicit qualification-test line items (Sheikh et al.)
developer: Hamad Bin Khalifa University (Sheikh, Hadid, Padmanabhan, Elomri, Kerbache, Alabtah, Khraisheh)
description: Total part cost is the sum of design, material, manufacturing (print, debind, sinter), post-processing and 'part qualification' cost. The qualification term sums per-part tests for dimensions, corrosion, strength, hardness and density.
NRE_note: A design cost term is included in the total cost equation.
Production_note: Material, printing/debinding/sintering and post-processing (heat treatment, machining, finishing) modeled per part.
QA_Qual_note: Labelled 'qualification', but it covers only per-part tests. There is no material/process qualification campaign or certification approval.
QA_Insp_note: Per-part test costs: dimensional $30, corrosion $50, strength $40, hardness $25, density $20, totalling $120–165, which is about 20% (impeller) and 11% (gear) of part cost. How the unit test costs were derived is not explained.
Storage_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capital_note: Upgraded on opening the paper: printing and debinding costs charge machine depreciation per hour times each part's processing time, a crude amortization of capital with no utilization or volume input.
Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.
Speed_note: Not addressed.

name: ASTM E3166-20e1 Standard Guide for Nondestructive Examination of Metal Additively Manufactured Aerospace Parts After Build
developer: ASTM Committee E07
earlier_versions: ASTM E3166-20 (2020): original edition, now listed as historical; reissued as E3166-20e1 with an editorial change that the ASTM page does not describe.
description: Surveys established and emerging NDT methods (CT, eddy current, optical metrology, penetrant, process-compensated resonance testing, radiography, thermography, ultrasonics) against AM flaw types, with a method-versus-flaw table and factors for selecting methods.
NRE_note: Not addressed.
Production_note: Not addressed.
QA_Qual_note: Excludes process control, fracture-critical part management and accept/reject criteria (Sec. 1.12–1.14).
QA_Insp_note: Supports selecting NDE methods by flaw type, size, location, orientation and geometry, but does not recommend a course of action and gives no costs (Sec. 1.11, 4.10).
Storage_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capital_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.
Speed_note: Not addressed.

name: In-situ NDE (INDE) with probability-of-detection framework for L-PBF (ORNL; Snow et al.)
developer: Oak Ridge National Laboratory (Snow, Scime, Ziabari, Fisher, Paquit)
description: Detects 200–1000 µm subsurface flaws from fused process-monitoring data using machine learning, with XCT as ground truth, and generates POD/PFA curves and an a90/95 metric following NDE practice, so in-situ monitoring can be assessed as an inspection method.
NRE_note: Not addressed.
Production_note: Not addressed.
QA_Qual_note: Only the abstract was read; it presents in-situ NDE as an alternative to costly ex-situ inspection, so whether the paper addresses qualification or certification is not established.
QA_Insp_note: Quantifies detection capability (POD comparable to traditional NDE). Claims in-situ monitoring is a 'less expensive alternative' to ex-situ testing, but gives no cost or time figures (abstract).
Storage_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capital_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.
Speed_note: Not addressed.

name: VEXTEC VPS-MICRO model-assisted AM certification (AFWERX SBIR; AFRL QUASAR)
developer: VEXTEC Corporation
description: Probabilistic microstructure- and defect-based fatigue software. It aims to predict EIDS distributions and part performance from specimen-level data so that part-level testing can be limited to validation ('risk-based certification').
NRE_note: Only company posts describe the tool; one says it reduces development time and cost by optimizing design and manufacturing, so whether it treats engineering effort is not established.
Production_note: Not addressed.
QA_Qual_note: Intended to reduce part-level qualification testing via model-assisted qualification. No quantified test, cost or time reduction is claimed (VEXTEC posts 2022–2024).
QA_Insp_note: Company pages say the model uses layer-by-layer machine sensor data, but whether it addresses or reduces per-part inspection is not shown.
Storage_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capital_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.
Speed_note: A 2024 company post says testing burden delays AM part availability, but no source shows the tool valuing lead time.

name: Joint Additive Manufacturing Acceptability (JAMA) framework, Phase II
year: Unknown (NCMS announcement undated; page last modified 22 Oct 2024)
developer: U.S. Air Force with NCMS (CTMA program), industry and academia
description: Develops a streamlined acceptance framework for AM products and a joint common framework for Qualified Parts/Manufacturers List specifications across 'JAMA risk categories'.
NRE_note: Only an NCMS project announcement describes the framework, and it does not say whether design or engineering effort is treated.
Production_note: The announcement says partners will supply 'cost analysis' support but describes no cost model, so whether production cost is treated is not established.
QA_Qual_note: Risk-category-based acceptance framework and QPL/QML structure; categories not defined on the page.
QA_Insp_note: Only a project announcement exists; it does not say whether the acceptance framework sets per-part inspection or testing.
Storage_note: The documented scope (a product-acceptance framework feeding QPL specifications) excludes spare-part inventory.
Shared_Capital_note: Reuse of one qualification through a QPL/QML across procurements was the earlier researcher's inference; the announcement does not state it.
Shared_Capacity_note: Only a project announcement exists; whether a joint QPL framework treats pooling qualified suppliers or capacity is not stated.
Speed_note: The announcement calls the framework 'streamlined' but does not say whether lead time or acceptance time is addressed.

name: NASA-CMU Additive Manufacturing Ecosystem for qualification of AM processes and materials in aviation
developer: NASA Ames Research Center (K. Datta) and Carnegie Mellon University (A. Rollett)
description: A six-project research ecosystem for qualifying AM machines, which then supports certification of part production. It names qualification difficulty and cost as the main barriers.
NRE_note: Only a TechPort project summary was read; its six projects target barriers to process qualification and efficient production, so whether engineering effort is treated is not established.
Production_note: The summary names the cost of the technology as a barrier and targets efficient production, but whether any project treats production cost is not shown.
QA_Qual_note: Qualitative framework linking machine/process qualification to part certification (NTRS abstract).
QA_Insp_note: Only a project summary was read, and it does not say whether per-part inspection is addressed.
Storage_note: Not addressed.
Shared_Capital_note: That machine qualification spreads across many certified parts was the earlier researcher's inference; the summary does not state it.
Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.
Speed_note: Not addressed.

name: 3DXpert (build preparation with print time and cost estimation)
year: Estimation feature documented 2019; 'Cost estimation and reports' still listed Feb 2026
developer: Developed by 3D Systems (TCT ties it to the 2015 Cimatron acquisition). On 1 Oct 2025, 3D Systems agreed to sell 3DXpert and Oqton MOS to Hubb Global Holdings, with closing expected Q4 2025. 3D Systems' FY2025 10-K says it 'divested of the 3DXpert business in 2025'. Feb 2026 product material is issued by Oqton Inc.
description: Metal AM build-prep software (part positioning, supports, lattices, print strategies). Its Estimation Parameters dialog computes print time from published build rates (part/support/lattice rates, recoat time). It then costs material per cm3 and machine time at an hourly rate, reporting volume, time and cost for parts, supports and lattices plus total powder required.
NRE_note: Automates build preparation (platform arrangement, supports, print strategies), but preparation effort is not costed (3DXpert Introduction 2026).
Production_note: Material cost (per cm3) plus machine time cost (hourly rate x total time) for parts, supports and lattices; labor and post-processing not included (3DXpert estimation guide 2019).
QA_Qual_note: The 2019 estimation guide and 2026 product pages do not address qualification effort; the product page only mentions inspecting and certifying builds for future comparison.
QA_Insp_note: The 3DXpert product page lists an 'AM Inspection' capability to inspect and correct anomalies and defects in builds, but inspection is not costed (oqton.com/3dxpert, 2026).
Storage_note: 3DXpert is build-preparation software for individual builds, so spare-part inventory is outside its documented scope.
Shared_Capital_note: Machine cost enters only as a user-supplied hourly rate over build time; no amortization or utilization model (3DXpert estimation guide 2019).
Shared_Capacity_note: As build-preparation software for a single machine's builds, 3DXpert does not address capacity pooled across sites or users.
Speed_note: Print time is estimated, but not lead time or the value of earlier availability.

name: Ansys Additive Prep (Cost Estimator)
developer: Ansys, now part of Synopsys (ansys.com product pages redirect to ansys.synopsys.com); Additive Prep runs inside Ansys SpaceClaim
description: Build-preparation tool whose Cost Estimator prices the whole build job. Machine cost comes from build time (laser path and jump times plus recoater time per layer). Material is powder volume over the baseplate area times part height, times density, plus a material-loss %. A profit margin is added. Output is an 'Estimated Total Price' exportable to CSV.
NRE_note: Supports and scan-pattern build files are generated here, but preparation effort is not costed (Ansys help 2024 R2).
Production_note: Build-job cost from scan-path build time, machine cost, powder use with loss % and profit; build-level total, no per-part split (Ansys help 2024 R2).
QA_Qual_note: The cost-estimator help lists only machine, material and profit terms, and Additive Prep's documented build-preparation scope does not include qualification.
QA_Insp_note: The cost-estimator help lists only machine, material and profit terms, with no inspection step.
Storage_note: Additive Prep prepares and prices single build jobs, so inventory is outside its documented scope.
Shared_Capital_note: Machine cost (largest contributor) is spread over everything in the build volume, so packing more parts lowers unit cost implicitly; no amortization or utilization inputs documented (Ansys help 2024 R2).
Shared_Capacity_note: Additive Prep prices one build job on one machine and does not address capacity shared across sites or users.
Speed_note: The help computes build time only to cost the machine and does not output lead time or a value of earlier delivery.

name: Ansys Granta Selector (Additive Manufacturing data)
year: Senvol integration announced May 2016; AM Edition in CES Selector 2019; AM data still listed in 2026 R1 help
developer: Granta Design (now Ansys Granta Selector; ansys.com redirects to ansys.synopsys.com); AM machine/material data from Senvol LLC
earlier_versions: CES Selector with Senvol data (May 2016): Granta Design first integrated Senvol machine and material data (550+ machines, 700+ materials) into CES Selector and GRANTA MI. | CES Selector 2019 Additive Manufacturing Edition (2019): Granta Design release covering >950 AM machines, >1,700 materials and >190 conventional equivalents from the updated Senvol Database; now sold as Ansys Granta Selector.
description: Materials/process selection software. The AM Edition embeds Senvol machine and material data. Users can filter machines by process, manufacturer, required part size, cost and compatible materials, and chart AM properties against conventional equivalents to judge whether AM is viable. A generic Part Cost Estimator gives relative costs (+/-20%) across processes, but AM coverage is not documented.
NRE_note: Granta Selector is a materials and process selection tool, so redesign, digitization and parameter-development effort are outside its documented scope.
Production_note: The Part Cost Estimator help does not list which processes it covers, so whether it estimates AM part cost is unknown.
QA_Qual_note: Compares AM vs conventional material properties; data mainly manufacturer-published and room-temperature only; no qualification burden (machinebuilding.net 2016; TMD 2019).
QA_Insp_note: As a materials and process selection database, Granta Selector does not address per-part inspection.
Storage_note: As a materials and process selection database, Granta Selector does not address inventory.
Shared_Capital_note: Machines can be compared by 'cost' (purchase price) as a selection criterion; no amortization or utilization (3DPI 2016; machinebuilding.net 2016).
Shared_Capacity_note: As a materials and process selection database, Granta Selector does not address production capacity.
Speed_note: As a materials and process selection database, Granta Selector does not estimate lead time.

name: Ansys Granta MI:Additive Manufacturing
developer: Granta Design (acquired by Ansys; ansys.com product pages now redirect to ansys.synopsys.com)
description: Enterprise database package for AM data. It stores process parameters and logged build data, links supplier information to material batches, and exports properties to simulation. Since 2016 it also exposes the Senvol machine/material database next to a company's own AM data for search and comparison.
NRE_note: Only a 2015 release describes the tool; it says process parameters are stored but not whether parameter-development or redesign effort is tracked or costed.
Production_note: The 2015 release does not mention part cost, and no product documentation was read.
QA_Qual_note: Captures process parameters, build logs and supplier-to-material-batch links, which form a record base for qualification; no qualification effort or cost modeled (DE 2015).
QA_Insp_note: The 2015 release does not mention test or inspection data, which a materials data system could plausibly hold.
Storage_note: Granta MI:Additive Manufacturing is a materials and process data management system, so spare-part inventory is outside its documented scope.
Shared_Capital_note: Senvol machine data, including a machine cost field, is searchable in GRANTA MI; no amortization (3DPI 2016).
Shared_Capacity_note: As a data management system it does not address production capacity shared across sites or users.
Speed_note: As a data management system it does not estimate lead time or the value of faster delivery.

name: Altair Inspire Print3D
developer: Altair Engineering (solidThinking unit at launch); altair.com product pages now redirect to siemens.com (ownership change not separately verified here)
description: SLM design and process-simulation tool. It generates and edits supports with the part, picks orientations that minimize supports, runs a thermo-mechanical solver (build, cooling, cutting, springback), flags deformation, overheating and delamination, and exports a print-ready file. No cost-estimation function was found in fetched sources.
NRE_note: Support generation, orientation and process simulation reduce trial builds and build-prep effort; not costed (3DPI 2019; CIMdata 2019).
Production_note: Launch coverage and the Inspire 2022.2 Print Part help page mention no cost estimate, but full product documentation was not read, so a cost function cannot be ruled out.
QA_Qual_note: Sources describe defect plots from the thermo-mechanical solver but do not say whether qualification effort is addressed.
QA_Insp_note: Launch coverage and the help index do not mention inspection, and full documentation was not read.
Storage_note: Inspire Print3D is a design and print-simulation tool for SLM builds, so inventory is outside its documented scope.
Shared_Capital_note: No source read describes a machine-rate or utilization input, but full documentation was not available to confirm absence.
Shared_Capacity_note: As a single-build design and simulation tool, it does not address capacity shared across sites or users.

name: Hexagon Simufact Additive (print cost estimation; part of HxGN Additive Manufacturing Suite)

description: Metal AM process simulation. It predicts and compensates distortion, residual stress and temperature. Its PBF Process and Defect Analysis module anticipates warping, porosity and incomplete fusion. It also estimates print-job costs for single components or assemblies, extending to downstream cutting, machining, drilling and grinding, to pick the best build variant.

Production_note: Estimates print-job cost for single components or assemblies incl. subsequent machining steps; cost inputs not documented publicly (Hexagon 2019).
QA_Qual_note: The Nexus page and 2019 release describe defect prediction (porosity, incomplete fusion) but do not say whether qualification effort is addressed.
QA_Insp_note: The Nexus page and releases do not mention inspection, and no product documentation was read.

Shared_Capital_note: The 2019 release says print-job costs are estimated, but its cost inputs, including any machine rate, are not public.

Speed_note: The 2019 release says print-job costs are estimated, but sources do not say whether print time or lead time is output.

name: Siemens NX Parts Order Management (AM and CNC job costing/quoting)
year: Current product page (2026). The URL of the 2018 Siemens Additive Manufacturing Network now 302-redirects here; Siemens does not state the relationship.
developer: Siemens Digital Industries Software

It claims 'flexible cost calculations to accurately price CNC machining and additive manufacturing jobs'. No AM-specific cost function was found in Teamcenter Product Cost Management or NX AM.

name: Ulu-Huang-Kara-Whitefoot (CMU) concurrent structure + process-parameter optimization for minimum-cost metal AM
developer: E. Ulu, R. Huang, L. B. Kara, K. S. Whitefoot (Carnegie Mellon University, Mechanical Engineering)
description: Couples a process-based cost model (material with 1% scrap, machine investment and maintenance amortised over 7 yr at 7,000 h/yr, energy, labour, 3.5% reject factor) with SIMP topology optimisation. Beam power is chosen per element, so structure and process parameters are optimised together for minimum cost under compliance constraints. Concurrent optimisation cuts cost by up to ~15% and build time by ~21% vs. structure-only optimisation.
NRE_note: Design, build-preparation and parameter-development effort are not costed. The tool automates part of DfAM, but its cost is not counted (author PDF).
Production_note: Per-part cost from build time (scan passes, power, velocity), material, energy and labour; e.g. bracket $675 to $575 (author PDF, Table 3).
QA_Qual_note: Not addressed (author PDF).

Storage_note: Not addressed.

Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.

name: Nie-Jung-Kara-Whitefoot (CMU) part-consolidation optimization for minimum production cost/time with metal AM
developer: Z. Nie, S. Jung, L. B. Kara, K. S. Whitefoot (Carnegie Mellon University)
description: Generates consolidation candidates from an interface connectivity matrix and removes structurally redundant ones with a 'closed-loop filter'. It then optimises build orientation for minimum support, places parts with a 2-D bottom-left layout, and estimates cost or time; a genetic algorithm searches large assemblies. Consolidating 17 components into 4 parts minimises cost (~20% lower unit cost); merging into 2 parts minimises time (~25%). Full consolidation is rarely optimal because support material and removal costs rise.
NRE_note: Redesign and engineering effort for consolidated parts is not costed (CMU PDF).
Production_note: Unit cost from part and support material, machine and maintenance, scrap, energy, setup, support removal, plus assembly (machining, riveting) for unconsolidated interfaces (CMU PDF).
QA_Qual_note: Not addressed (CMU PDF).
QA_Insp_note: Inspection is not modelled (CMU PDF).
Storage_note: Inventory is explicitly excluded. Fewer part numbers could cut spares inventory, but this is not modelled (CMU PDF).
Shared_Capital_note: Machine cost is an hourly rate (amortised equipment, maintenance, labour) times build time, and setup cost depends on the number of batches from the plate layout; utilisation and sharing with other part numbers are not modelled (CMU PDF).
Shared_Capacity_note: Not addressed.
Speed_note: Unit production time is an alternative objective (time-optimal consolidation). Time is not dollarised or tied to when parts are needed (CMU PDF).

name: Piili et al. (LUT/Aalto) laser PBF stainless-steel cost estimation by build scenario
developer: H. Piili, A. Happonen, T. Väistö, V. Venkataramanan, J. Partanen, A. Salminen (affiliations not shown on the accessed record; record held by Aalto University)

Machine investment dominates while energy and material are minor, so time per part is the main lever. A secondary review reports that building as many parts as possible per build cut cost 81-92% vs. building singly.

name: Barclift et al. (Penn State) CAD-integrated cost estimation and build-orientation optimization for metal PBF
developer: M. Barclift, A. Armstrong, T. W. Simpson, S. B. Joshi (Pennsylvania State University)
description: Pulls part volume and surfaces through the SolidWorks API and generates internal and external supports as solid bodies, then varies build orientation. This lets designers estimate build time and feedstock (including depreciation of reused powder) while designing. An imprecise support angle underestimates support volume by 34% and build time by 20%. Poor orientation and packing can push powder-depreciation cost to nearly twice the material cost.
NRE_note: Only the abstract was read; it automates support generation and orientation but does not say whether design or build-preparation labour is costed, and the 2016 base model does cost per-part geometry preparation.
Production_note: Build time and feedstock, including supports and powder depreciation, per part (Penn State abstract).

name: Reiher et al. (Paderborn DMRC) holistic approach: part selection through test and verification
developer: T. Reiher, C. Lindemann, U. Jahnke, G. Deppe, R. Koch (Paderborn University, DMRC)
description: Chains the TOM selection matrix (rough cost quote, knock-out criteria, scored sub-criteria) with topology-optimisation redesign, a manufacturing strategy (orientation, supports, thermal stress) and part marking. It adds a three-tier test scheme: part-independent material/process tests, witness specimens in every build, and part-specific NDT (CT, dimensional, surface) plus load tests. The bracket was 60% lighter with buy-to-fly reduced from ~50 to 1.5. AM was cheaper at the forecast volume, although post-processing and quality costs 'had a major impact'.
NRE_note: Redesign workflow (FE topology optimisation, voxel smoothing, NURBS) is defined, but its effort is not costed (Springer PDF).

name: Siller et al. (TU Berlin) potential-assessment and adaptation method for AM of conventionally made components
developer: N. Siller, S. Werner, V. Molina, D. Göhlich (Technische Universität Berlin, Institute of Machine Design and Systems Technology)
description: A pass/fail prefilter (fits build space, material available, AM-sensitive features acceptable, no legal restriction, conventional production not much cheaper) is followed by 0-4 scored assessments. These cover in-process and post-process restrictions and 'opportunistic' economic, eco-social and functional drivers, weighted by utility analysis. An automatic 'AM adaptation potential' flags parts that minor redesign could make suitable. Below 40% overall means low suitability; above 65% means generally suitable. In the case, 5 of 11 parts failed the prefilter.
NRE_note: The adaptation-potential score flags where minor redesign would help, but redesign effort is not costed (Springer full text).
